Laura (CS): Quick sanity check on Helix dedicated pool after overnight spike. Sharing 7d rolling and an ops plan.

CapacityBot: ALERT: pool "helix-dedicated" saturation hit 92% for 14m at 03:57 UTC. Queue depth 18 recorded. Creating INF-4910.

Ben (SRE): Saw the reroutes. Autoscale didn't kick due to reserved-capacity cap. I'm pulling scheduler + autoscaler traces now.

Kevin (Eng Runtime): Can you grab 95th percentile token latency and model variant histogram? Suspect long-context onboarding jobs are causing KV cache growth.

Laura (CS): Quick numbers (7d window):
GPU hours: 4,080 (-11% W/W)
Saturation: avg 65% | peak 92%
Queue depth: median 3 | 95th 19
Top tenants by GPU hrs: helix 44%, polara 17%, newbloom 9%
Active alerts: helix soft-overage x2
Renewal risk: elevated — customer alarmed by night alerts

Tina (Acct Mgmt): Helix got soft-limit emails. They're worried about surprise spend and will ask about guarantees on our Fri renewal prep call. I need remediation options ASAP.

Ben (SRE): Short-term: 1) spin up a 48h burst pool (+4 GPUs) for helix; 2) add a rate-limit on onboarding ETL tasks; 3) short-circuit heavy jobs to a lower-cost model during spikes. I'll open INF-4910 and attach logs.

Kevin (Eng Runtime): Early findings: onboarding is using a non-quantized model with 32k context and heavy prefixing. If they switch to 8-bit quant and trim prefix for batch runs we can save ~25-35% GPU hours.

Laura (CS): Action items: Ben -> INF ticket + scheduler traces; Kevin -> quantify KV-cache footprint and propose config toggles; Tina -> confirm Helix will join Fri 15:00 PDT call and agree to test a throttled run.

CapacityBot: INF-4910 created by Ben (SRE). Alert thresholds adjusted: helix-dedicated new warn at 85% with 10m suppression.

Tina (Acct Mgmt): Confirmed call Fri 15:00 PDT. I'll ask them to run a paused ETL for 24h or move to off-peak while we test. Want to keep renewal path healthy.

Laura (CS): Thanks team — I'll send a customer-facing note once Ben/Kevin post the ticket + recommended config. Ben, paste the INF link here when available. :thumbsup:
